newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian trade fair records low turnout, chaos.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian trade fair records low turnout, chaos.

text.p: An international trade fair characterised by low turnout and chaos opened on Friday in Nigeria's commercial hub of Lagos.
Makeshift stalls were still being built at the fair complex as airforce chief Air-Vice Marshall Nsikak Eduok declared it open on behalf of military ruler General Sani Abacha.

"The chaos will ease off and things will take shape but the low turnout of exhibitors this year worries us," Abiodun Adefehinti, spokesman for the Lagos Chambers of Commerce, the organisers of the fair, told Reuters.
Almost 300 exhibitors will participate in the 10-day fair this year compared with 550 last year.
Kola Daisi, chairman of the fair organisers, said they believed the country needed new economic measures.
"More bolder measures are needed to stimulate the economy and jump-start it to favourable growth next year," he said.
Nigeria's economy, the biggest in Sub-Saharan Africa, slumped into recession when the army annulled an election in 1993 to restore democracy, resulting in strikes and riots.
Some pragmatic economic policies in place since 1995 have stabilised the economy but with few signs of growth yet.
